reading.body:
OpenColo's Santa Clara facility publishes 9 MW of total capacity, with 4.5 MW described as coming soon. The phrasing on the operator's site leaves ambiguous whether this means 4.5 MW is currently online or will be online shortly, so the total figure cannot be treated as a firm committed number. The facility occupies 71,000 square feet. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW of IT load would be roughly 225 racks; at 100 kW per rack, a denser configuration for high-end accelerator clusters, it would be roughly 90 racks.

The facility holds SOC 2 Type II certification, which qualifies it to process data subject to compliance audits. Backup power includes dual utility feeds, 2.75 MW of diesel generation, lithium-ion batteries, and indirect evaporative cooling with N+1 redundancy. The operator publishes a 100 percent uptime SLA.

In California, which has 103 mapped data center facilities, only 11 operators publish megawatt figures in their public specs. OpenColo's Santa Clara site does not rank in the state's top 11 by published capacity, placing 12th among the 11 published capacities. California's disclosed facilities total 365 MW across those 11 operators. This campus represents a smaller, mid-market colocation facility, not a hyperscale hub.
